questions.q: A family that cannot pay for food this month.
questions.a: Yes: the poor and the needy (9:60).

questions.q: A man who owes money he cannot repay.
A rich friend who wants a new phone.
questions.a: No: zakah is not for the rich.

questions.q: A traveller stranded far from home with no money.

questions.a: Not one of the eight groups in 9:60: use sadaqah instead.

blocks.h: My sadaqah plan for the week

cols: My sadaqah (money, help or a kind word)

keywords.def: the poor: people with very little
the needy: people who cannot meet their needs
any charity or good deed given freely

questions.q: Explain two differences between zakah and sadaqah.
questions.a: Zakah is compulsory at 2.5% on savings above nisab for the eight groups; sadaqah is voluntary, any amount, to anyone.

questions.q: Name three of the eight groups.
questions.a: For example: the poor, the needy, the traveller

questions.q: Zakah quiz and case cards on the pupil PDF: decide whether each person may receive zakah (example cases), then write a sadaqah plan for your week.
questions.a: Correct decisions using 9:60; a realistic sadaqah plan

questions.q: Extend: why does Allah list the recipients Himself?
questions.a: So zakah reaches the right people fairly.

questions.q: Stretch: name one good cause that could be 'in the way of Allah'.
questions.a: For example: spreading knowledge of Islam (scholars differ on what is included)

options: Anyone can give it, any time
questions.a: A) Anyone can give it, any time. Sadaqah is voluntary and can be any good deed.

questions.q: Think again: who should get it first?
questions.a: Those Allah names in 9:60, such as the poor and needy.
